key_insight: Conservative finite-volume discretisation naturally retains the full Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes viscous terms, delivering DNS-level accuracy without separately discretising the second Brinkman term.
engineering_relevance: DBS2 enables accurate digital-rock flow and permeability prediction directly on voxelised micro-CT images while preserving DBS1 computational efficiency.
method: Express the full DBS equation in conservative form.
Apply standard central differencing in a finite-volume discretisation.
Implement DBS2 in GeoChemFoam and compare against DNS.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmarks, DBS2 exactly reproduced the microchannel DNS velocity field and matched micromodel and Bentheimer sandstone DNS permeability within 1.5–3.8% at matched resolution; DBS1 overpredicted permeability by 14.1–37.9%.
watch_item: Validation covers three benchmark cases; accuracy on other rock geometries and at coarser voxel resolutions remains to be established.
paper_title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for Digital Rock Flow Simulation with Embedded Second-Brinkman Effects
